synthesis.summary: The app's content layer is genuinely strong — the reading hero, one-tap highlight capture, InlineReflection, comfort devotions, pathway lessons, and the AI tone are all better than typical church software — but three load-bearing layers underneath it are quietly failing the 144 real users. (1) Data safety: the sync stack has multiple verified permanent-loss paths, the worst being a reinstall/transient-error wipe of the user's only cloud backup (DS-01/DW-F03) and a one-tap highlights mass-delete after any sync (DS-02); pastoral prayer data is exposed by an unauthenticated PCO endpoint and an over-scoped analytics dashboard. (2) The daily loop: streak math runs on UTC against the repo's own local-date invariant and silently punishes evening readers; the commuter listen path degrades at four layers (poisoned 5,000-char preload cache, ESV audio 502ing on ordinary Gospel chapters, stale chapter index every morning, no Media Session); completion is marked on Stop but the plan-finish celebration is swallowed. (3) The entry: the church origin serves 404 pages as Library content, wipes the /listen PWA's caches on every visit, sells a nonexistent email product with a fabricated 300k subscriber figure, and the rebuilt two-gate onboarding buries each persona's promised content behind 2-8 setup decisions. Everything in fix_now and ux_ship_now below is implementable this session without touching the owner-locked look, the localStorage-first data model, or any stated invariant; the onboarding restructure, church-site copy/canon, IA renames, and translated pastoral content need Ashley's call.

fix_now.title: Stop sync from wiping the only backup on pull failure
fix_now.plan: Server: return 404 only for PostgREST no-rows code PGRST116, 500 for every other select error; on push, refuse to overwrite a non-empty stored journal with an empty [] (same empty-guard for highlights/streak/plans — this reinforces, not violates, the journal invariant). Client: pullFromCloud rethrows non-404 failures; syncOnStartup takes the first-time 'initial backup' push branch ONLY on a true 404; on pull failure set a pull-never-succeeded flag that suppresses/queues schedulePush and flushNow for the session and retries the pull with backoff. Optionally send lastSyncVersion on push as groundwork for compare-and-swap.

First tap after a sync currently erases the entire restored/other-device set and pushes the loss to the cloud.

One-time tolerance on upgrade: treat stored lastDate matching either the local or UTC rendering of today/yesterday as a match so no existing streak breaks. Replace the month-relative freeze week key with a true ISO week or a stored lastFreeze date ('replenish if 7+ days since'). Apply the same en-CA fix to PlansScreen.streakDisplay and dw_first_open.

fix_now.title: Un-break the listen path: poisoned preload cache + ESV audio over the 6MB cap

confirmed.title: Pull failure is treated as 'no cloud data' — unmerged (or empty fresh-install) local state is pushed over the user's only backup
confirmed.detail: pullFromCloud() returns null on ANY error (cloudSync.ts:352-363 catches everything: 429 rate-limit, 500, timeout, network), and the server also maps ANY Supabase select error to 404 'No data found' (netlify/functions/user-sync.js:206-212 `if (error || !data)` — a transient DB/pool error is indistinguishable from a truly missing row). syncOnStartup() then takes the first-time-user branch (cloudSync.ts:419-423) and pushes local state as 'initial backup'; even if that immediate push fails, the journal merge never happened for the whole session, so every later debounced push (schedulePush, flushNow) overwrites the cloud with unmerged local data. Failure scenario: user reinstalls the app / gets a new phone, enters their email, and the startup pull hits a transient error or the 30/min-per-IP rate limit (user-sync.js:26-38 — shared church-WiFi NAT on a Sunday can trip this); collectLocalData() on the fresh install returns journal:[], highlights:{}, misc:{} etc., validatePayload accepts them all (user-sync.js:104-131), and the upsert (user-sync.js:247-250) plus the misc replace (user-sync.js:274) wipe the cloud row — journal, prayed-for, sermon notes, My Season, streak — permanently, at the exact moment the backup was the only copy. There is no sync_version compare-and-swap anywhere: lastSyncVersion is stored (cloudSync.ts:134, 373) but never sent or checked.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Distinguish 'no account data' from 'pull failed'. Server: only return 404 for the PostgREST no-rows code (PGRST116); return 500 for other errors. Client: have pullFromCloud rethrow non-404 failures; in syncOnStartup, if the pull FAILED (vs genuine 404), skip the first-backup push, set a 'pull never succeeded' flag, and suppress/queue all pushes for the session (retry the pull with backoff) until one pull has succeeded. Additionally send lastSyncVersion on push and have the server refuse a push whose payload journal is empty when the stored row's journal is non-empty unless a pull happened first (cheap tombstone against the wipe).
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified in code. pullFromCloud returns null on ANY throw (cloudSync.ts:360-362) and on !success/!data; server maps every select error to 404 via `if (error || !data)` (user-sync.js:206), so a transient DB/pool error, a 429 rate-limit, or a true miss are indistinguishable. syncOnStartup then takes the first-time branch (419-423) and pushes. On a fresh install collectLocalData returns journal:[], highlights:{}, streak:{}, etc.; validatePayload accepts all of them (Array.isArray([]) and typeof {}==='object' both pass), and the upsert (247-250) plus the misc replace `update({misc})` (274) overwrite the existing cloud row's journal/highlights/streak/plans/sermon-notes/prayed-for with empties. No sync_version is ever sent on push (lastSyncVersion stored at 134/373, never in the body), so there is no compare-and-swap. Catastrophic loss of the only backup at reinstall time is real and reachable; P0 honest. Proposed fix (404 only for PGRST116, distinguish pull-fail from empty, suppress pushes until one pull succeeds) does not touch the journal-merge-authoritative invariant.

confirmed.title: Highlights context never refreshes after cloud sync — first toggle after sync writes the stale pre-sync map and mass-deletes highlights everywhere
confirmed.detail: ScriptureSelectionProvider loads dw_highlights into React state once at mount (`useState<...>(loadHighlights)` line 136) and has NO listener for dw-cloud-sync. The provider mounts ABOVE the sync remount boundary — App.tsx keys only `<main key={syncNonce}>` (App.tsx:261) while the provider wraps everything (App.tsx:337) — so when syncOnStartup's applyCloudData rewrites dw_highlights from the cloud (cloudSync.ts:186-201), the in-memory map stays pre-sync. toggleHighlight then derives the next map from that stale state and writes it wholesale: `localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(next))` (line 155) + schedulePush (line 167). Failure scenario: phone+iPad user; iPad opens Sunday, startup sync overwrites iPad's week-old local map with the phone's current 50-highlight map, but provider state still holds the old map; user taps ONE highlight → dw_highlights becomes old-map+1, the phone's week of highlights is erased locally and pushed to the cloud; the phone's next startup pull wholesale-overwrites its local map (cloud non-empty branch, cloudSync.ts:190-192) → highlights permanently destroyed on every device. On a fresh install the state is {} at mount, so one tap after the restore erases the entire restored set.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In ScriptureSelectionProvider add a dw-cloud-sync listener that re-runs loadHighlights() into state (mirroring PlansScreen.tsx:134-141), and make toggleHighlight read-modify-write against localStorage (read current map inside the updater, like the journal helpers do) instead of trusting in-memory state, so a missed event can never cause a wholesale regression.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified. ScriptureSelectionProvider seeds highlights once via useState(loadHighlights) (ScriptureSelectionContext.tsx:136) and has NO dw-cloud-sync listener. The provider wraps AppContent (App.tsx:337) ABOVE the remount boundary — only `<main key={syncNonce}>` remounts (App.tsx:261) — so applyCloudData's wholesale rewrite of dw_highlights (cloudSync.ts:186-201) leaves the in-memory map stale for the session. toggleHighlight derives next from stale `prev` and writes it wholesale to localStorage (line 155) then schedulePush (167), so one tap after a sync-restore erases the restored set and pushes the regression; the other device's next non-empty pull wholesale-overwrites its local map. PlansScreen has the mirror listener the provider lacks. Mechanism and cross-device permanence are real. Severity is at the aggressive end (highlights are study data, not pastoral prayer) but it is silent permanent data loss that propagates, so P0 is defensible, not dishonest.

confirmed.title: Journal editors never stamp updatedAt — the equal-timestamp 'longer body wins' merge rule systematically reverts and permanently loses shortening edits
confirmed.detail: The main journal editor saveEntry (JournalScreen.tsx:1534-1546) writes `all[idx] = editingEntry` with no updatedAt; handleTodaySave (1506-1512), ScriptureModal handleSave (`{ ...existingNote, body: draftNote }`, JournalScreen.tsx:705-706), the sermon-outline save (MessagesScreen.tsx:517-528 — which also never calls schedulePush, only the dw-journal-updated event), and one BibleAI save path (BibleAI.tsx:~290-305) all create/edit entries without updatedAt (only VerseNoteDrawer.tsx:42/62/78, InlineReflection.tsx:50, BibleAI.tsx:341 and the tombstone writers stamp it). mergeJournals falls back to `date` — a day-granular string — so an edited entry and its pre-edit cloud copy compare EQUAL (cloudSync.ts:275-279), landing in the conflict branch where the LONGER body wins (cloudSync.ts:283-294). Failure scenario: entry synced to two devices; user rewrites a long rambling note into a shorter one on device A and it pushes; device B's next startup merges cloud(short) vs local(old long) with equal timestamps → the OLD long version wins on B and is pushed back; A's next pull restores the old text — the user's edit is permanently reverted, with a spurious conflict toast. Same loss on one device whenever a shortening edit didn't reach the cloud before the next startup merge (offline, killed within the 5s debounce).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Stamp `updatedAt: new Date().toISOString()` at every journal write site — saveEntry, handleTodaySave/ScriptureModal handleSave, the MessagesScreen sermon save (and add its missing schedulePush), and the BibleAI ~300 path — ideally by routing all of them through one shared write helper so future call sites can't regress. The tombstone-merge logic itself needs no change.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified. saveEntry writes `all[idx] = editingEntry` with no updatedAt (JournalScreen.tsx:1534-1543); handleTodaySave sets all[idx]=entry unchanged; ScriptureModal handleSave builds `{ ...existingNote, body: draftNote }` with no updatedAt (705-706); the MessagesScreen sermon save creates an entry with no updatedAt AND only dispatches dw-journal-updated (no schedulePush) (517-527); BibleAI saveToJournal (291-299) omits updatedAt while saveStudyToJournal stamps it (341). Journal entries carry only a day-granular `date` ('August 25, 2026'), so mergeJournals falls to `existing.updatedAt || existing.date` and an edited entry vs its pre-edit copy compare EQUAL (cloudSync.ts:275-276), entering the conflict branch where longer body wins (283-294). A shortening edit therefore loses to the old long version and is permanently reverted with a spurious conflict toast. Real silent data loss; P1 honest.

confirmed.title: applyCloudData wholesale-overwrites highlights/streak/bookPlans/reactions/pathwayProgress with the cloud copy — offline or concurrent-device changes are destroyed on every startup
confirmed.detail: For the jsonFields list (cloudSync.ts:179-201), any non-empty cloud value replaces the local value with no per-entry merge, no timestamps and no version check (the string prefs at 225-238 behave the same). Only journal and activePlans get real merges. Failure scenarios: (1) user highlights verses / earns streak days while offline (pushes fail silently, cloudSync.ts:375-377); next app start pulls the older cloud copy → cloud non-empty → local overwritten → merged-away work is then pushed back, making the loss permanent. (2) Two devices open the same morning: A records today's streak and pushes count=10; B pulled before that and later pushes its post-pull copy (count=9, lastDate=yesterday) — last write wins, cloud regresses to 9; if A doesn't open again until two days later its local 10 is overwritten by 9/stale-lastDate and the streak chain breaks to 1. Highlights suffer the same add-vs-remove clobber (a cleared/changed map on one device resurrects or erases entries on the other, compounding DS-02).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Give the wholesale fields the same treatment activePlans got, without touching the journal invariant: union-merge highlights by verseKey keeping the newer `timestamp` field each entry already carries; merge streak by keeping the state with the later lastDate (and max count on equal dates); merge bookPlans per bookId by higher currentChapter; merge reactions/pathwayProgress per key by progress. Longer term, send lastSyncVersion on push and let the server reject stale writes so concurrent devices converge instead of ping-pong overwriting.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified. applyCloudData's jsonFields loop replaces local highlights/streak/bookPlans/reactions/pathwayProgress with any non-empty cloud value, with no per-entry merge, timestamp, or version check (cloudSync.ts:178-201); string prefs behave the same (233-238). Only journal and activePlans get real merges. Offline changes push silently-fail (pushToCloud catch, 375-377), so the next startup pulls the older cloud copy and overwrites local, and the merged-away work is then pushed back permanently; concurrent-device streak/highlight edits clobber last-write-wins. Reachable and real. Proposed per-field union/newest-wins merges keep journal out of jsonFields, so no invariant is violated. P1 honest.

confirmed.title: applyMisc applies ANY key from the cloud misc bag — no whitelist, so a stale client or anyone with an email-issued token can overwrite dw_profile, dw_session_token, or dw_journal on the victim's devices
confirmed.detail: collectMisc filters to MISC_KEYS + MISC_PREFIXES (cloudSync.ts:82-95), but applyMisc iterates every entry in the cloud bag and writes it straight into localStorage (cloudSync.ts:110-123) — fill when local-empty, or newest-wins for any non-authored key using cloud-supplied dw_misc_meta stamps (line 120). The server accepts up to 300 ARBITRARY key names into misc (user-sync.js:269-274, only length caps). Failure scenario: any client that can push to the account — including an old app version with a different sweep list, or a third party who obtained a session token via the unverified email-based migrateRequest (netlify/functions/lib/auth.js:122-145) — plants `dw_profile` (different email) plus an inflated stamp in dw_misc_meta; the victim's next syncOnStartup writes it, silently re-pointing all future pushes (journal, prayer data) at another account, or clobbers dw_journal (not authored, not prefix-protected — a direct violation of the journal-merge-is-authoritative invariant via the side door). dw_session_token is equally writable.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In applyMisc, skip any key that is not MISC_META_KEY, not in MISC_KEYS, and not matched by MISC_PREFIXES — the exact filter collectMisc uses (extract it to a shared predicate). Optionally enforce the same whitelist server-side in the misc write loop (user-sync.js:269-272) so the bag can never carry foreign keys at all.
confirmed.verify_reason: The core technical claim is verifiably true: collectMisc filters to MISC_KEYS/MISC_PREFIXES/meta (cloudSync.ts:82-95) but applyMisc iterates EVERY cloud-bag entry and writes it to localStorage, skipping only MISC_META_KEY (110-123) — no whitelist. The server stores up to 300 arbitrary key names in misc (user-sync.js:269-271). So dw_profile/dw_session_token/dw_journal placed in the cloud bag are written to a victim device, re-pointing pushes or bypassing the journal tombstone-merge invariant via the side door. Note honestly: in pure current-client normal operation collectMisc never emits those keys, so the trigger requires a non-standard pusher — an old/divergent client sweep list, or a token obtained via the deliberately-weak email migrateRequest (auth.js:122-137). The attacker path overlaps the accepted weak-auth model, so this reads primarily as defense-in-depth hardening; but the code deviation is real, the fix (reuse collectMisc's predicate) is cheap and strengthens the fill-only + journal-authoritative invariants. P1 defensible given pastoral data.

confirmed.title: Keepalive flush gate counts UTF-16 chars, not bytes — Spanish/Portuguese users' close-time flushes silently fail once the payload passes ~21-60KB of multibyte text
confirmed.detail: `const keepalive = !!opts?.keepalive && body.length < 60000` measures string length; the browser's 64KiB keepalive quota is BYTES of the encoded body. A journal full of accented es/pt-BR text encodes ~1.1-2x, and non-Latin content up to 3x: a 45,000-char body can be ~70-90KB encoded, so fetch(..., {keepalive:true}) rejects immediately with TypeError, pushToCloud swallows it (cloudSync.ts:375-377), and the visibilitychange/pagehide flush (main.tsx:36-46) does nothing — every session-end backup for that user silently fails while smaller users' flushes work, until some foreground debounced push happens to run. Data written in the last 5s before close is never backed up for exactly the heaviest journal users.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Gate on encoded size: `new Blob([body]).size < 60000` (or TextEncoder().encode(body).length), and when the keepalive path is refused for size, fall back to navigator.sendBeacon where available, else fire the normal fetch as today.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified. `const keepalive = !!opts?.keepalive && body.length < 60000` (cloudSync.ts:330) gates on UTF-16 string length; the browser keepalive quota is 64KiB of the ENCODED body. Multibyte es/pt/id content encodes 1.1-3x, so a <60000-char body can exceed 64KB bytes, fetch({keepalive:true}) rejects with TypeError, pushToCloud swallows it (375-377), and the visibilitychange/pagehide flush (main.tsx:43-46) silently no-ops for exactly the heaviest journal users. The CLAUDE.md gotcha even documents the 60KB margin, which is char-based and insufficient for multibyte. Fix (Blob/TextEncoder byte size + sendBeacon fallback) is sound and invariant-safe. P2 honest.

confirmed.title: isSyncing collisions silently drop pushes with no retry — including the flush on app close and syncOnStartup's push-back of the merged state
confirmed.detail: pushToCloud early-returns when a push is in flight (`if (!email || isSyncing) return;` cloudSync.ts:367) and nothing reschedules. Failure scenarios: (1) user saves an entry (debounced push starts at t+5s, in flight for 1-2s), then backgrounds the app inside that window — tryFlushSync → flushSync → pushToCloud returns immediately, so edits made after the in-flight push's collectLocalData() are never flushed and the app may be killed. (2) During syncOnStartup, any user action in the first seconds schedules a push; if it is in flight when line 438's `await pushToCloud(email)` runs, the merged journal/misc state is NOT pushed back — and the in-flight push contained PRE-merge local data, so cloud-only journal entries temporarily vanish from the backup until some later successful push from this device.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Replace the boolean drop with coalescing: if a push is in flight, record a pending-dirty flag (with the keepalive option OR-ed in) and run one follow-up push in the finally block; have flushSync await the in-flight push then push again. Keep the guard's reentrancy protection — just never discard the request.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified. pushToCloud early-returns on `if (!email || isSyncing) return;` (cloudSync.ts:367) with no rescheduling. flushSync (background/close) calls pushToCloud directly, so if a debounced push is in flight the flush no-ops and edits written after that push's collectLocalData are not backed up before a possible kill; during syncOnStartup an in-flight user push makes the line-438 merged push-back a no-op. Both are real coalescing gaps. Windows are narrow (in-flight is ~1-2s; most losses recover on the next successful push from the same device) and permanent loss needs a kill/clear before that, so P2 is at the generous end but the mechanism is genuine. Fix (pending-dirty flag + follow-up push in finally) is safe.

confirmed.title: Server truncates each misc value at 20,000 chars — sermon notes / My Season / prayed-for become invalid JSON in the cloud and restore as empty on a new device
confirmed.detail: `misc[k] = typeof v === 'string' ? v.slice(0, 20000) : v` (user-sync.js:271) silently cuts any misc value mid-string; `Object.entries(miscIn).slice(0, 300)` (line 269) silently drops keys past 300. dw_sermon_notes is ONE key holding every sermon note (MessagesScreen.tsx:806) and dw_user_story is free text — both plausibly exceed 20,000 chars over years of use. The truncated string is no longer parseable JSON, so on reinstall/new device applyMisc fills it (cloudSync.ts:115-117), the reader's JSON.parse fails to [] (e.g. sermon-notes load), and the user's notes appear gone; the new device then pushes the corrupt/empty value onward. The client is never told anything was cut (the 5,000-entry journal cap at line 104 has the same silent-drop shape but keeps valid JSON).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Never truncate mid-value: if a misc value exceeds the cap, keep the EXISTING stored value for that key (skip the update) and return a warning field in the response the client can surface; raise the per-key cap for the known-large authored keys (dw_sermon_notes, dw_user_story) or split sermon notes to per-id dw_sermon_ keys which are already prefix-swept. Same skip-don't-slice treatment for the 300-key cap.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified. `misc[k] = typeof v === 'string' ? v.slice(0, 20000) : v` truncates any misc value mid-string (user-sync.js:271) and `Object.entries(miscIn).slice(0, 300)` drops keys past 300 (269), both silently. dw_sermon_notes is a single key holding the whole JSON array of notes (MessagesScreen.tsx:806) and dw_user_story is free text; either can exceed 20000 chars for an active user. Truncated mid-array is unparseable, so on a new device applyMisc fills the corrupt value (cloudSync.ts:115-117), the reader's JSON.parse fails to [] and notes appear gone, then the device pushes the empty/corrupt value onward. Skip-don't-slice fix is correct. P2 honest.

confirmed.title: Quitting a plan resurrects it: activePlans union-merge has no tombstones, so any other device (or an offline quit) restores the removed plan
confirmed.detail: applyCloudData union-merges cloud+local activePlans keeping every plan from both sides (cloudSync.ts:207-223 — deliberate so sync never drops a plan). resetPlan deletes the plan and flushes (PlansScreen.tsx:284-305, flushNow at 291), which covers only the same-device-online race. Failure scenarios: (1) user quits a plan on the phone (cloud updated), opens the iPad later — iPad's startup union re-adds the plan from its local copy and line 438 pushes it back; the phone's next startup union resurrects it there. The quit can never stick while a second device exists. (2) Quit while offline: flushNow fails silently, next startup unions the cloud copy back on the SAME device. bookPlans resurrect the same way via the wholesale non-empty overwrite (cloudSync.ts:181,190-192) against resetPlan's dw_book_plans removal (PlansScreen.tsx:297-301).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Keep the union invariant but make quits explicit: instead of deleting the map entry, write `{ ...prog, removed: true, removedAt: Date.now() }` as a plan tombstone; in the union-merge prefer a removed marker with newer removedAt over a live copy (and vice-versa if the live copy has newer progress), prune removed markers after a TTL like the journal's 180 days; filter removed plans from every reader (getActivePlans already centralizes this). Mirror for bookPlans.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified. applyCloudData union-merges activePlans keeping every plan from both sides with no tombstone (cloudSync.ts:207-223). resetPlan deletes the key and flushNow (PlansScreen.tsx:284-305), which only covers the same-device-online race; a second device's local copy re-adds the plan on its next startup union and line-438 pushes it back, so a quit can never stick while another device exists, and an offline quit is unioned back on the same device. bookPlans resurrect via the wholesale non-empty overwrite. The proposed plan-tombstone fix preserves the deliberate union invariant (never drop a one-device plan) while letting explicit quits stick — consistent with the deletes-are-tombstones invariant. P2 honest.

confirmed.title: Streak day-boundary logic uses UTC toISOString dates — evening/morning US usage burns freezes and resets streaks despite daily engagement; freeze week key collides across months
confirmed.detail: recordStreakToday computes today/yesterday/day-before with `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` (streak.ts:36, 43, 45) — UTC — while the repo rule (and the rest of the day logic, e.g. HomeScreen.tsx:304, 568) is LOCAL dates via toLocaleDateString('en-CA'). For US users (UTC-4/5), any engagement after ~7-8pm lands on the NEXT UTC day. Failure scenario: engage Mon 8am (Mon UTC), then Tue 9pm (Wed UTC) — both local days covered, but lastDate=Mon vs today=Wed is a 2-day UTC gap, so the weekly freeze is spent (lines 55-58); a second evening/morning alternation the same week resets the streak to 1 (line 60) even though the user engaged every single local day. confirmed.title: Tombstone-prune guard is defeated by Date parsing: a tombstone with no updatedAt gets timestamp ~2000 and is pruned immediately instead of retained

confirmed.title: push reminder delivery has no catch-up: a skipped cron hour or a null preferred_hour silently drops the day's reminder
confirmed.detail: The timezone model itself is correct: push-cron runs @hourly in UTC and push-send computes each subscriber's LOCAL hour via Intl.DateTimeFormat(timeZone) and matches currentHour === preferred_hour (line 253), so hourly firing covers every timezone — this structurally answers 'what timezone does the cron fire in'. Two edge gaps remain: (1) matching is exact-hour with a 1-hour granularity and no catch-up window, so if Netlify delays/skips a scheduled run (scheduled functions are best-effort) the subscribers whose local hour was that hour get NO reminder that day. (2) legacy/edge rows where preferred_hour is null never satisfy `currentHour !== null` and are skipped forever (push-subscribe defaults to 7, so this only affects rows created by other paths). Half-hour-offset zones (e.g. Asia/Kolkata) fire at :30 past the target hour — cosmetic. None cause data loss; delivery reliability only.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add a catch-up window (e.g. fire if it is preferred_hour AND no send is recorded for this subscriber today, using a last_sent_date column to also prevent duplicates), and coalesce null preferred_hour to a default (7) in the query or comparison.
confirmed.verify_reason: Code-verified and honestly scoped. push-cron is @hourly UTC and push-send computes each subscriber's LOCAL hour via getCurrentHour(sub.timezone) and matches currentHour !== sub.preferred_hour -> skip (line 253), so hourly firing structurally covers every timezone (correctly answering the timezone question). The two edge gaps hold: (1) exact-hour match with no catch-up window / last_sent_date, so a skipped/delayed best-effort scheduled run drops that hour's cohort for the day; (2) a null preferred_hour never equals the numeric currentHour so those rows are skipped forever (push-subscribe defaults to 7, so only non-standard rows are affected, as stated). Finding correctly notes these are delivery-reliability only, no data loss — honest P3. Catch-up-window + null-coalesce fix is valid and invariant-neutral.

confirmed.title: Streak logic runs on UTC dates (toISOString slices) — violates the LOCAL-date invariant and breaks streaks for evening readers
confirmed.detail: recordStreakToday() computes today/yesterday/day-before via new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) (lines 36, 43, 45) — the UTC day, not the user's calendar day. The load-bearing invariant says plan/reading-day logic uses LOCAL dates via toLocaleDateString('en-CA'), never UTC toISOString slices. Verified: at 9pm America/New_York on 2026-08-25, en-CA local date is 2026-08-25 but the UTC slice is 2026-08-26. Failure scenarios for US users (the app's core audience): (a) read Mon 7am ET (lastDate=Mon UTC), read again Tue 9pm ET (today=Wed UTC) → two consecutive LOCAL days, but UTC sees a gap → the weekly freeze is burned, or if none left the streak RESETS to 1; (b) open the app Mon 10am and again Mon 9pm ET → two increments in one local day (the mount effect HomeScreen.tsx:539 calls recordStreakToday on every open), then Tue morning is a silent no-op — 'idempotent per calendar day' is false across the 8pm ET boundary. The axis is also mixed against dw_reading_done, which is en-CA local (HomeScreen.tsx:304/482), so 'Read today ✓' and the streak counter can disagree. Same UTC slices in PlansScreen.tsx streakDisplay() (lines 96-98) and dw_first_open (HomeScreen.tsx:554). Additionally, inside recordStreakToday the week key mixes axes ('thisWeek' uses LOCAL getDate() while 'today' is UTC) and the key format `${year}-W${ceil(date/7)}` repeats each month (week 4 of Aug == week 4 of Sep), so a spent freeze can fail to replenish.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In streak.ts, compute today as new Date().toLocaleDateString('en-CA'); derive yesterday/day-before by date arithmetic (d.setDate(d.getDate()-1)) then .toLocaleDateString('en-CA'). Add a one-time transparent migration: when comparing raw.lastDate, treat a lastDate equal to either the local or UTC rendering of today/yesterday as matching so no existing streak breaks on upgrade. Make the week key unambiguous (e.g. ISO year-week or `${y}-${m}-W${ceil(d/7)}`) and derive it from the same local axis. Apply the same en-CA fix to PlansScreen.streakDisplay() and dw_first_open.
confirmed.verify_reason: streak.ts lines 36/43/45 use new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) (UTC) exactly as claimed, while dw_reading_done (HomeScreen 304/482), the rollover (755), and dw_plan_day_offset (152) use toLocaleDateString('en-CA') local — a direct violation of the LOCAL-date invariant for reading-day logic ('Record today as a reading day', HomeScreen 538-539 calls recordStreakToday on every mount). Node check verified 9pm ET local=2026-08-25 vs UTC slice=2026-08-26, so both failure scenarios (freeze burned/streak reset across a two-local-day span; double increment in one local day then next-morning no-op) are reachable for US users. Supplementary claims all verified: PlansScreen streakDisplay (94-100) uses the same UTC slices, dw_first_open (554) is a UTC slice, and the week key `${getFullYear()}-W${ceil(getDate()/7)}` (line 37) mixes the local axis against the UTC 'today' and repeats each month (2026-W4 in Aug == Sep), so a spent freeze can fail to replenish. P0 is honest under the stated rule that an invariant violation is automatically P0.

confirmed.detail: calcPlanDay (HomeScreen.tsx:111-122, duplicated PlansScreen.tsx:106-117) does new Date(startedAt). confirmed.title: Hero Listen shows no loading state and fails silently: onStateChange's synchronous replay of 'idle' instantly settles the guarded-unsub pattern
confirmed.detail: AP.onStateChange(fn) invokes fn synchronously with the CURRENT state on subscribe (audioPlayer.ts:58-62). In handleHeroListen (and handleHeroSkipTo, lines 1159-1169), the state at subscribe time is 'idle' (nothing has called setState yet — playChapterAtIndex is fire-and-forget and awaits fetchPassage first), so the branch `st === 'idle' && !AP.isLoading()` fires immediately: setHeroLoading(false) cancels the setHeroLoading(true) from line 1117 in the same tick and the listener is removed at line 1141. Result: (1) the play button never shows the spinner during the 1-5s fetchPassage+fetchAudioSrc window, defeating the explicit 'Show loading IMMEDIATELY so user sees feedback on tap' intent; (2) the duplicate-tap guard `if (AP.isLoading() || heroLoading) return` (line 1093) is inert during that window, so the natural second tap bumps heroChainVersionRef and restarts the chain. Compounding: when every chapter fails to produce audio (offline, or all providers down), the chain exhausts by resolving normally — the outer .catch never fires, audioError is never set, and even if it were, the error line (1742) is gated on audioCurrentPassage === HERO_KEY which is still null because no state change ever carried the hero key. Net: offline, tapping the primary hero Play button does visibly nothing, forever, with no message. This is the same defect class as the TDZ-unsub trap — the guard fix (lines 1140-1141) correctly avoids the null-unsub crash but converted it into an instant-settle logic bug.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In both handleHeroListen and handleHeroSkipTo, only treat 'idle' as terminal after the chain has been seen active — mirror waitForEnd's sawActive pattern: let sawActive=false; in the callback set sawActive on 'loading'/'playing', and only clear heroLoading + unsubscribe on ('playing') or (sawActive && 'idle'). Separately, have playChapterAtIndex signal exhaustion (return a boolean or call a callback when index >= heroChapterRefs.length without any successful playUrl) and set audioError(true) there; change the error-line gate at 1742 to show on audioError regardless of audioCurrentPassage (or set setAudioCurrentPassage(HERO_KEY) on failure).

In handleHeroListen's uncached path, playChapterAtIndex suspends at await fetchPassage (1024) with AP state still 'idle', so the subscription at 1133 fires immediately with ('idle', !isLoading) → setHeroLoading(false) in the same tick as setHeroLoading(true) (React batches; spinner never renders) and the guarded-unsub (1140-1141) removes the listener. The duplicate-tap guard (1093) is then inert during the fetch window and a second tap bumps heroChainVersionRef, killing the chain. (In the cached-src path playUrl sets 'loading' synchronously before the subscribe, so the bug is specific to the uncached path — matching the finding's own reasoning.) Exhaustion verified: all-fail chains return normally via the index>=length branch (1010-1012), .catch at 1128 never fires, no setState ever carries HERO_KEY so audioCurrentPassage stays null and the error line at 1742 (gated on audioCurrentPassage===HERO_KEY) can never show. Offline hero Play is a silent no-op.

confirmed.title: Background audio preload caches a 5,000-char clip under the full-chapter cache key — TTS audio cuts off mid-chapter
confirmed.detail: The preload effect calls AP.fetchAudioSrc(text.slice(0, 5000), translation, passage) (line 684). fetchAudio's cache key is `${passageRef}_${translation}` (api.ts:240) — it ignores the text — and the result is also stored in the component-level audioSrcCache. handleAudio later requests text.slice(0, 20000) (line 815) and the hero chain requests the FULL text (line 1027), but both hit the poisoned key first and play the 5,000-char clip. Failure scenario: any user on a TTS-served translation (KJV, NKJV, NIV, AMP, NASB, WEB — and ALL Spanish/Portuguese/Indonesian translations, which are TTS-only) opens the app with an active plan; the preload fires as soon as text loads; they tap Listen on a chapter longer than ~5,000 chars (Psalm 119, most Gospels chapters, Genesis narrative chapters) and the audio stops roughly a third of the way through the chapter with no error. ESV is usually exempt (native audio fetched by ref), but if esv-audio is down during preload, the truncated ElevenLabs/Polly clip is cached for ESV too.

More robust: include a discriminator in fetchAudio's cache key (e.g. `${passageRef}_${translation}_${text.length}` or a cheap hash) so differing inputs can't collide.

For TTS-served translations (everything except ESV native; verified _doFetchAudio routes KJV/NKJV/NIV/AMP/NASB/WEB and all non-English to ElevenLabs/Polly on the text) the cached blob is audio of only the first 5,000 chars, so chapters longer than that cut off mid-chapter. confirmed.title: Restart button leaves heroLoading=true for the entire playback chain — pause becomes impossible and the button spins while audio plays
confirmed.detail: The Restart handler runs playChapterAtIndex(0, rv).catch(...).finally(() => setHeroLoading(false)). playChapterAtIndex's promise only resolves when the whole multi-chapter chain ENDS (it awaits playUrl, then waitForEnd, then recursively the next chapters), so the .finally fires at the end of playback, not when audio starts. From the tap on Restart until the last chapter finishes: isLoadingHero stays true, the big hero button renders a spinner instead of Pause (aria-label 'Loading audio'), and handleHeroListen's gate `if (AP.isLoading() || heroLoading) return` (line 1093) makes the hero button, the full-plate tap target, and the spacebar shortcut all dead — the user cannot pause; only the footer Stop works. handleHeroListen/handleHeroSkipTo use the onStateChange subscription for this instead (which has its own bug, SCRIPT-03); Restart uses neither correctly.

So heroLoading stays true for the entire playback: isLoadingHero (1520) renders the spinner with aria-label 'Loading audio' (1626, 1642-1643) instead of Pause, and handleHeroListen's gate (1093) makes the labelled hero button, the full-plate tap target (1590), and the spacebar handler (1173-1183) all early-return. confirmed.title: Localized book-plan JSON paths double-suffix and the SPA fallback returns 200 HTML — book plans broken for Spanish/Portuguese (start) and all non-English (advance)
confirmed.detail: startBookPlan stores plan.jsonFile = localizedBookJsonFile(book.jsonFile) (line 152) — e.g. '/books/scarcity_id.json' — and HomeScreen.startPlanFromHome does the same (lines 896-899). advanceBookChapter then calls fetchBookJson(plan.jsonFile) (line 178), which re-applies the suffix: '/books/scarcity_id_id.json'. confirmed.title: chaptersPerDay pulls N plan-DAYS, not N chapters — multi-chapter plans balloon 'today' to 10-16 chapters
confirmed.detail: todaysPlanPassages interprets chaptersPerDay as a count of consecutive plan DAYS (numPassages loop over dayIdx = dn-1+offset, lines 629-637), then splits each day's comma-joined passages. For one-chapter-per-day plans that coincidentally equals chapters, but through-bible-year and new-testament-90 pack 3-4 chapters per day (genPassages), so the default chaptersPerDay=3 (line 269) yields ~10-12 chapters queued as 'today' — labeled Day N, N+1, N+2 — and each is eagerly fetched (heroChapterRefs effect line 932) plus audio-preloaded (line 675), multiplying ESV/TTS function invocations and cost. confirmed.title: Midnight crossing while the app stays focused never rolls the plan day — no timer backs up the focus/visibility listeners
confirmed.detail: The #45 rollover effect (754-786) fires rollIfNewDay only on visibilitychange and window focus. Mobile PWA resume paths are covered (visibilitychange), which is why this is P3 not P2.

If the window stays visible and focused across midnight neither event fires; window 'focus' does not fire from in-page interaction when the window already has focus. confirmed.title: ListenButton's 'Pause' control actually stops and discards position; a paused state restarts from zero
confirmed.detail: The component is documented as a 'Play/Pause toggle' and titles the playing state 'Pause' (line 143), but handleClick calls AP.stop() when playing (lines 50-53), which discards the blob and position. confirmed.title: esv-audio base64-encodes whole-chapter MP3s into the function response — the longest chapters likely exceed Netlify's response payload cap and silently degrade to TTS
confirmed.detail: The function buffers the full ESV MP3 and returns it base64-encoded (line 104), inflating size ~33%, and also caches up to 20 such bodies in memory (CACHE_MAX=20). Netlify synchronous functions cap the response payload (~6MB; this project has previously hit the related 4.5MB body cap per the repo's operational history). Psalm 119 (176 verses, ~15 min of audio) plausibly exceeds the cap after base64, in which case the platform rejects the response after the handler returns: the client's _tryESVAudio gets a failed response and silently falls back to ElevenLabs/Polly TTS (api.ts:267-269 → 311-321) — losing the human reader for exactly the marquee long chapters, with the 3-attempt/7s-timeout retry loop burning function time first. Not confirmed at runtime (marked plausible); the psalms-proverbs plan serves 'Psalms 119' as a normal day, so the path is reachable.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Verify with a live curl of /api/esv-audio?q=Psalm+119 (response size/status). If over the cap, stream instead of buffering: return a 302 redirect to the ESV audio URL (audio.esv.org is already allowed in media-src CSP) or proxy via a signed short-TTL URL, avoiding base64 entirely; also drop such oversized bodies from the in-memory cache.
confirmed.verify_reason: Code claims verified (full buffer + base64 at esv-audio.js 103-104, CACHE_MAX=20 in-memory cache of base64 bodies, retry loop), and the runtime hypothesis was proven by live curl: GET https://futuresdailyword.com/api/esv-audio?q=Psalm+119 returns HTTP 502 with body {"errorType":"Function.ResponseSizeTooLarge","errorMessage":"Response payload size exceeded maximum allowed payload size (6291556 bytes)"} — and Luke 11 and John 11 fail identically, while Psalm 117 succeeds at ~197KB. So the cap is real (6,291,556 bytes), the failure is broader than the finding's 'longest chapters' framing (ordinary Gospel chapters exceed it too), and the client's _tryESVAudio (api.ts 327-345) sees !res.ok and silently falls back to ElevenLabs/Polly TTS exactly as described. If anything the P3 severity is understated, since much of the ESV 'Human Reader' catalogue is currently unservable; the 302-redirect fix is compatible with the existing media-src CSP (audio.esv.org already allowed in netlify.toml).

confirmed.title: DW registers a scope-'/' service worker on futures.church every visit — each /daily-word pageview wipes ALL church-origin caches (including the /listen offline shell), and the fdw_nuked block unregisters the /listen worker
confirmed.detail: Answering 'does the SW try to register on the church origin and is it a no-op': registration IS attempted unconditionally — main.tsx:73-76 runs `navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js?v=v65', { scope: '/' })` with no hostname gate. On futures.church that resolves to the church's own kill-switch public/sw.js (live-verified; /sw.js correctly stays un-proxied per the invariant). Registration SUCCEEDS (no console.warn, no broken /daily-word, push already hostname-gated in push.ts, and the kill-switch never calls clients.claim() so the controllerchange->reload never fires) — so it is SILENT, but it is NOT side-effect-free: the kill-switch's activate handler deletes EVERY Cache Storage key on the futures.church origin, then unregisters itself — so the next /daily-word pageview re-registers it and wipes again, every visit, forever. That deletes 'listen-shell-v2', the offline app-shell cache of the church's /listen audiobook PWA (futures-church-web/public/listen/sw.js), breaking offline listening for any congregant who opens /daily-word between /listen visits (chapters in IndexedDB survive but the shell can't load offline). Separately, index.html's fdw_nuked block (lines 128-146) runs un-gated on the church origin once per version bump: `getRegistrations().forEach(unregister)` kills ALL registrations on futures.church including the /listen-scoped worker, deletes all caches except fdw-bible-v1/fdw-fonts-v1, and forces a reload 500ms into the user's first /daily-word visit. push.ts's own comment ('the church-proxied build deliberately ships NONE') confirms registration there was never intended.

Do NOT re-proxy /sw.js — the kill-switch stays; this fix simply stops re-arming it on every view.
confirmed.verify_reason: main.tsx:73-98 registers /sw.js?v=v65 with scope '/' unconditionally — no hostname gate (contrast pushSupported() in push.ts:60-71, which gates exactly as described, and push.ts:53 carries the quoted 'deliberately ships NONE' comment). On futures.church, /sw.js live-serves the 1,055 B kill-switch (futures-church-web/public/sw.js), whose activate handler deletes ALL cache keys on the origin then self-unregisters (lines 18-26) — including 'listen-shell-v2' (public/listen/sw.js:19, whose own hygiene only touches 'listen-'-prefixed keys); self-unregistration means every subsequent /daily-word pageview re-registers and re-wipes. confirmed.title: SW offline-navigation fallback has a dead branch, and offline.html is dead weight (never built, never referenced)
confirmed.detail: sw.js:141 `.catch(() => caches.match('/') || caches.match(event.request))` — caches.match() returns a Promise, which is always truthy, so `|| caches.match(event.request)` can never execute; and if '/' is missing from STATIC_CACHE (storage-pressure eviction, failed install addAll) the respondWith resolves to undefined and the offline user gets the browser's generic network-error page. Normally '/' is pre-cached so this is an edge case. Relatedly, offline.html exists in the repo root but is (a) not in vite.config.ts's copy list and not in public/, so it never reaches dist — live-verified: https://futuresdailyword.com/offline.html serves the 9,078-byte SPA shell via the SPA fallback — and (b) never referenced by sw.js anyway (the fallback is the cached '/'). The branded offline page (with its dark-green palette, which also predates the reskin) is unreachable dead code.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Fix the fallback chain: `.catch(() => caches.match('/').then((r) => r || caches.match(event.request)))`. Then either delete offline.html, or (nicer offline UX) restyle it to the ivory/terracotta look, add it to PRE_CACHE and the vite copy list, and make it the final fallback when '/' is uncached. Bump the SW cache-name suffix when changing sw.js.
confirmed.verify_reason: sw.js:141 is exactly `.catch(() => caches.match('/') || caches.match(event.request))` — caches.match() returns a Promise, always truthy, so the right operand is unreachable, and if '/' is uncached the respondWith resolves undefined and the navigation fails with the browser error page. '/' is in PRE_CACHE (lines 15-18) so it is an eviction/failed-install edge case — P3 is the honest severity. offline.html: exists at repo root, has zero references in sw.js (grep count 0), is absent from vite.config.ts's copy list (line 28) and from public/, and live futuresdailyword.com/offline.html serves the 9,078 B SPA shell via SPA fallback — dead weight as claimed. Fix (then-chain + either delete or restyle-to-ivory-and-precache, bump cache suffix) is correct and invariant-safe.

confirmed.title: Update flow force-reloads open tabs mid-session (and gives first-time visitors up to two automatic reloads)
confirmed.detail: main.tsx messages SKIP_WAITING to every newly installed SW (lines 79-92) and reloads on controllerchange (line 108-110); sw.js calls clients.claim() on activate. So: (1) any prod deploy reloads every open tab within the 30-minute update-check window — if a user is mid-keystroke in a journal or prayer entry that has not hit its save path, the text is gone, and data loss is this app's #1 risk; (2) a brand-new visitor's first SW install claims the page and fires controllerchange -> reload, stacking with the one-time fdw_nuked reload (index.html:145) for up to two automatic reloads on first visit. The SW v22 changelog claims 'gentle postMessage, no forced reload', but the page-side controllerchange handler re-adds the forced reload — the SW_UPDATED message handler (main.tsx:101-105) is an empty no-op. DW-origin only (the church kill-switch never claims, so no reload there).

This preserves fast updates without yanking a page out from under a typing user.

ux.flow_walkthrough:
RETURNING USER WITH AN ACTIVE PLAN — what the code actually does (all paths verified in /Users/ashleymarkevans/futures-daily-word-audit, commit 12861a48): 1. OPEN APP. HomeScreen mounts. A mount effect (HomeScreen.tsx:539) calls recordStreakToday() — the streak advances on OPENING the app, before any reading. If today hits 7/14/30/60/100/365 the fire-emoji milestone modal pops 600ms after launch (line 3627) — the milestone moment always precedes the reading, never follows the "done" tap. The streak counter + encouragement label ("Two weeks!") render top-right (hidden for new_to_faith/comfort); the persona greeting quotes the same count. 2. SCREEN ONE. The hero fills the viewport (minHeight 100svh-80px): a 16:10 photo plate (HeroPhotoCarousel, 6.5s crossfade) with the plan label ("Ashley & Jane — Day 41") top-left, the first chapter ref in 27px serif bottom-left, a 78px play button center, and — plan users only — 44px prev/next day chevrons flanking it. The entire photo plate is one big play button (invisible full-plate button, HomeScreen.tsx:1590). Below the plate: chapter slider + pills ("Chapter 1 of 3"), then a Read/Restart/translation footer. A read-first effect (line 993) auto-expands today's scripture into a white panel (maxHeight 60vh, nested scroll) — so "today's reading" is genuinely THE thing on screen one, zero taps to see the text. CAVEAT: dw_chapters_per_day defaults to '3' and SetupPromptModal is unreachable (setShowSetupModal(true) has no call sites), so a default-config user on a 1-chapter/day plan sees THREE plan days as "today" — and tomorrow 2 of those 3 chapters repeat. 3. YESTERDAY / TOMORROW: exactly 1 tap each via the hero chevrons (setPlanDayOffset ±1, clamped to day 1…totalDays; offset is date-keyed in dw_plan_day_offset and resets at local midnight; the #45 focus/visibility rollover correctly clicks the plan to the new day). BUT a second "TODAY'S READING" date-nav strip sits directly under the hero (line 2010) whose arrows move a DIFFERENT axis (dayOffset — the legacy daily-rotation used by quotes/word-of-day), unbounded into the past; for a plan user tapping it changes almost nothing visible yet the [dayOffset] effect (line 559) stops any playing audio and collapses the reading panel. 4. READ path: scripture is already open; per-verse tap-to-highlight (ScripturePassage), then InlineReflection ("What stood out to you…?" → textarea → saves straight into dw_journal, fires dw-journal-updated, pushNow(), counts streak) — a genuinely good in-context journal hand-off, though "Saved to your journal" is a dead confirmation with no link to the Journal tab. Below it, "Mark as read" (line 1947) → handleMarkRead: stamps dw_reading_done with the LOCAL date (en-CA — correct axis), marks the plan day complete, haptic, then DoneCelebration — a calm card ("Today's reading, done." / streak line / "Amen"), auto-dismissing in 3.6s. One global done per day: after marking, the button reads "✓ Read today" everywhere, including on yesterday's passage during catch-up. Note handleRead (line 508) ALSO silently marks the plan day complete on mere expansion, so the deliberate button is ceremonial for plan progress — and both handleRead and the audio chain DISCARD markPlanDayComplete's planFinished result while stamping finishedCelebrated=true, so finishing a whole plan by reading or listening swallows the finish-line celebration forever. 5. LISTEN path (commuters): 1 tap anywhere on the photo → handleHeroListen → iOS silence-blob unlock → chapter chain playChapterAtIndex: fetch text → TTS/ESV audio blob → play → waitForEnd → markPlanDayComplete(ref) → prefetch+advance to next chapter. Within-session pause/resume keeps position. BUT: (a) there is NO Media Session API anywhere in the repo — no lock-screen title/artwork/next-chapter control; (b) audioPlayer.ts only listens for 'ended' — an OS-level pause (phone call, headphones unplugged, lock-screen pause) leaves state 'playing' and the UI desynced; (c) heroChapterIndex persists in dw_hero_chapter_idx with no key check, so after listening through all 3 chapters yesterday, a cold open today starts BOTH the play chain AND the auto-opened read panel at today's LAST chapter (prevHeroKeyRef initializes to the current key, so the mount never resets a stale index); (d) Stop resets the index to 0, losing your place; (e) no cross-session within-chapter resume; (f) finishing the full audio never marks the day done — the only "Mark as read" lives at the bottom of the 60vh nested text scroll a listener never opens. 6. STREAK vs REAL LIFE: streak.ts computes today/yesterday/day-before with new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) — UTC — while dw_reading_done and the day rollover use local en-CA. A US-Eastern user reading Mon 7am (Mon UTC) then Tue 9:30pm (Wed UTC) skips a UTC day: the weekly freeze silently burns, and the same pattern again that week resets to 1 despite reading every local day; an 11:58pm read plus a next-morning read collapse into one UTC day. The freeze "week" is `${year}-W${ceil(date/7)}` — month-relative and missing the month, so replenishment misfires across month boundaries. Cloud restore (cloudSync.ts:180) blindly overwrites the local streak, racing the mount-effect recordStreakToday on a second device. A broken streak resets to 1 with no memory (no bestCount) and no acknowledgment. 7. WEEKLY REVIEW: WeeklyReviewCard renders only for pastor_leader (the sole persona with weeklyReview:true), only Sundays, only streak>=3, computed once at mount; daysRead is min(streak,7); its reflection question is a static

with no capture. Congregation — the core habit audience — never sees any weekly moment. 8. TOMORROW'S RETURN: push (push-cron/push-subscribe, gated by pushSupported() with calendar fallback) is the re-entry trigger; the loop's celebration/marking layer (DoneCelebration, milestone modal, Mark as read, weekly review) is hardcoded English even though es/pt-BR/id are shipped — t('mark_complete') exists in UI_STRINGS but the real button uses literal 'Mark as read'.

== FIRST RUN (both personas) ==
1. App.tsx: first launch shows PathwayPicker full-screen (needsFirstRunPicker gates on dw_v7_pathway_done). One screen, five cards, one tap. 2. Immediately after the pick, a SECOND full-screen gate renders: PushOptIn ("One gentle nudge a day", hour dropdown, red "Turn on daily reminders" / "Maybe later"). English-only. A person in crisis must dismiss this before seeing any comfort content. TAP 2 = skip or enable.
3. EmailGate does NOT auto-pop (action-triggered only, via requireEmail on write actions) — good.

== COMFORT PERSONA — what the code actually renders on Home (HomeScreen.tsx render order is HARD-CODED; sectionOrder is only used as a gate set via .includes(), so the config's intended order for comfort — verse banner 2nd, comfort_scripture 5th — is NOT honored) ==
1. Header: Bible AI pill + "Daily Word". Streak deliberately hidden for comfort + new_to_faith (line 1378) — good, no pressure.
2. Greeting (getGreeting): rotating warm lines — "You are not alone, {name}." Good tone. (en/id only; es/pt get English.)
3. HERO CARD (line 1473): with no active plan and no reading slots — the state of every fresh comfort user — the hero photo card reads "Choose your reading plan / Pick a plan and everything here syncs to your daily reading. / Browse Plans". heroChapterRefs (line 918) is built ONLY from todaysPlanPassages + readingSlots; the comfort rotation is never fed in. So the first thing a person in crisis sees is a setup task.
4. Dark date-nav bar ("TODAY'S READING" + date + prev/next arrows).
5. Full-width terracotta "Choose Your Plan" button (line 2063, unconditional for all personas) — 2nd setup CTA.
6. ComfortVerseBannerSection — one rotating verse (14-verse list, rotates on UTC day boundary: Math.floor(Date.now()/86400000)).
7. BibleAIPromptSection — "Talk to Bible AI about what you're feeling" (good copy; comfort AI system prompt is genuinely gentle and escalates to "talk to your pastor or a trusted friend").
8. ComfortCard — a second rotating verse card (12-verse list, 10 of 12 overlap the banner's list) + "Pray" button revealing a guided prayer that AUTO-CLOSES after 30 seconds (ComfortCard.tsx line 40-45) — ~70-word prayers, tight for a distressed slow reader.
9. Two dark book promo cards ("Grace & Truth", "No More Fear" — "RECOMMENDED").
10. UpgradePromptCard — after 30 days active: "Feeling Stronger? … No pressure — God's timing is perfect" (well-toned).

ONLY NOW (line 2326) ComfortSection — "A WORD FOR YOU TODAY / Take your time": the auto-loaded comfort chapter (Psalm 23 etc. from COMFORT_CHAPTERS), Listen button, then "Which words brought you the most peace?" → "I've finished reading" → an excellent short devotion (COMFORT_DEVOTIONS, en+id) → "Would you like to read another passage?" → after 3 chapters, "set a daily reading amount" (1/2/3 chapters). THIS is the heart of the persona and it renders ~9 blocks down, below both setup CTAs, the book promos and the upgrade card. Choosing a daily amount writes dw_comfort_daily and promises "You're set for N chapters a day. We'll have something ready for you tomorrow" — but NOTHING ever reads dw_comfort_daily (only cloudSync whitelists it): tomorrow serves exactly 1 chapter with the same tap-through regardless.
12. "TODAY'S CHAPTERS" section (comfort includes 'scripture') → for a plan-less user, an EMPTY STATE: "No reading plan active … Browse Plans" — a 3rd setup CTA, at the bottom of a comfort page.
All ComfortSection/ComfortCard/banner strings except the chapters_1-3 picker are hardcoded English.

== NEW_TO_FAITH PERSONA ==
On Home mount the 40-day Faith Pathway auto-enrolls silently (HomeScreen line 319-344: enrolled:true written to dw_pathway_progress, /books/faith-pathway.json fetched — file exists at repo root /books, deployed and returning 200 on prod). Zero-tap enrollment — good.
1. Header + "Welcome, {name}. We're glad you're here." No streak.
2. HERO = the same "Choose your reading plan / Browse Plans" setup card — the pathway reading (Day 1: Ephesians 2) does NOT feed the hero either, even though it is loaded via loadPassage (line 596-609).
3. Date nav + unconditional "Choose Your Plan" terracotta CTA.
4. Blue "YOUR FAITH JOURNEY — Day 1 of 40 — Grace Changes Everything … Continue →" banner (line 2099). Tapping it does getElementById('pathway-lesson-card') — that id exists NOWHERE in the codebase (only the getElementById call) — so it always falls through to onNavigate('plans'), navigating the new believer AWAY from their lesson which sits two blocks further down the same page.
5. "New here? Ask Bible AI anything … like having a friend who knows the Bible really well" — excellent copy.
6. NewBelieverLessonCard (line 2600): "DAY 1 OF 40", progress bar, lesson title/theme, full lesson text (warm, jargon-free, e.g. "grace isn't how you GET saved—it's how you LIVE saved"), 📖 Ephesians 2:8-9, Mark Complete / Share, then "TODAY'S READING" with translation pills + the full auto-loaded chapter + Listen. This is genuinely great content — but it is the 6th block on the page, below two plan-setup CTAs. Mark Complete instantly swaps in Day 2's lesson with no acknowledgment moment, and savePathwayProgress never calls recordStreakToday().
7. "TODAY'S CHAPTERS" empty state — 3rd "Browse Plans" CTA.
8. Plans tab: full catalogue sorted by PERSONA_PRIORITY (good), but the "RECOMMENDED FOR YOU — 30-Day Faith Pathway — Start Faith Pathway" card is at the very BOTTOM of the hub (line 1309), after all plans, both book sections, essays and the streak card. Starting it creates a SECOND, PARALLEL pathway: a 30-day scripture plan (catalogue id 'faith-pathway') competing with the auto-enrolled 40-day lesson pathway — two different "Day 1 of N" progress tracks with different content. persona-config's plans.autoSuggest ('faith-pathway' / 'psalms-brokenhearted') and featuredCategories are entirely dead config — never read anywhere; the categories they name ('beginner', 'devotional', 'topical') don't even exist in PLAN_CATALOGUE.

== VERDICT ==
Both personas have genuinely excellent CONTENT (comfort devotions, pathway lessons, AI tone, greetings, hidden streaks) but the PAGE ORDER inverts the promise: a crisis user and a brand-new believer each land on a plan-setup hero plus two more setup CTAs before reaching the content built for them, the comfort daily-amount promise is a no-op, the pathway banner's Continue is broken, and the comfort/new surfaces are the least internationalized in the app.

The Journal's Sermon tab shows the first plus the congregation fill-in — i.e. for the person PREACHING Sunday it shows "No sermon notes this week — check back before Sunday service." New Entry on that tab creates type:'journal', which then files under All Notes, not Sermon. The persona's 'teaching-notes' entry type has no creation UI anywhere.

PASTOR-ADMIN SURFACES (user-facing): Settings > ADMIN > Poll Results (persona-gated, code via window.prompt()); Settings > ADMINISTRATOR > App Analytics (PIN via prompt(); the server, analytics-dashboard.js:31, ALSO accepts campus pastor codes with real per-campus data, but the UI never says so); Campus > Pastor's Corner > "Post to Your Campus" (persona-gated form posting to campus-content with a pastor code typed as a password field every single time, never persisted, no hint where a code comes from). netlify/functions/pastor-admin.js (verify/post/delete/list-codes) has zero client callers — not user-facing.

WHERE THE IN-FLIGHT SERMON WORKSPACE SHOULD SLOT (flagging, not designing): (1) wizard step 13 "What are you preaching through?" is its natural intake — the answer should seed the workspace instead of dead-ending into a book plan; (2) HighlightToolbar/VerseNoteDrawer need a "file to current sermon" target so mid-study captures land in prep; (3) Journal > Sermon tab's "MY SERMON NOTES" section is where its output belongs, unifying the three stranded stores; (4) the PastoralReflectionSection slot on Home is where its "continue prep" card should surface.

Additionally make the Active Plans strip rows tappable (HomeScreen.tsx:3301 div has no onClick) -> onNavigate('plans'); that fixes the same dead end for every book plan started anywhere.

recommendations.title: Collapse the triple plan-CTA stack on the pre-plan pastor Home
recommendations.detail: A pastor with no plan sees three competing plan entry points in one viewport: the hero's 'Browse Plans' button, the unconditional 'Choose Your Plan' CTA (HomeScreen.tsx:2063 — it renders for every persona at all times, even with active plans), and the wizard card. The wizard — the one path with pastor-specific framing — is the LAST of the three, and the other two bypass it (and if the pastor starts a plan via Plans tab, the mounted wizard card still sits on Home asking to set them up). In PastorStudyOnboarding.tsx, re-check dw_activeplans on each render (not just the useState initializer) so the card self-dismisses once a plan exists.

recommendations.title: Move commentary next to the passage it comments on

The pastor's intended study cluster (passage -> pastoral prompt -> commentary) is split: the COMMENTARY card (HomeScreen.tsx:3142) renders after the daily quote, word-of-day and weekly review, 5+ cards below TODAY'S STUDY, and only for the day's FIRST passage. recommendations.title: Delete or implement the dead pastor persona wiring (congregation_stats, devotion, adminTools, plans config)

'leadership' / autoSuggest) is consumed nowhere — featuredCategories values don't even match real plan categories ('Books','Foundation','Life & Faith'...). recommendations.title: Reconnect the stranded Strongs pipeline (or retire it) for Greek/Hebrew word taps
recommendations.detail: Greek/Hebrew mode's word tap (HomeScreen.tsx renderScripture:1186) sends every word to Bible AI as a free-text prompt — online round-trip, AI cost, variable-quality answer — while a purpose-built fast path sits dead: GreekHebrewPopup.tsx + netlify/functions/strongs.js are unreachable because their only trigger (ScriptureBlock.tsx setActivePopupWord) is mounted nowhere. If token data is not obtainable, delete ScriptureBlock.tsx, GreekHebrewPopup.tsx, and strongs.js as dead code so the AI path is the honest single implementation. Either outcome removes a stranded half-system.

recommendations.title: Cut the pastor-code friction in Pastor's Corner and surface that pastor codes open real analytics
recommendations.detail: Posting to Pastor's Corner requires retyping the 8-char campus code into a password field on every post (MessagesScreen.tsx:271-282, component state only), with zero hint where a code comes from. Meanwhile Settings' 'App Analytics' (real per-campus data) is labeled ADMINISTRATOR with 'Enter administrator PIN' via window.prompt(), even though analytics-dashboard.js:31 explicitly accepts campus pastor codes — pastors who hold a code don't know it unlocks their real numbers (which is also the credible data source for PL-01). The window.prompt() entry is jarring in an otherwise polished PWA and prompt() can be suppressed in some standalone-PWA contexts.
recommendations.concrete_change: In MessagesScreen.tsx: on first successful post, persist the code (localStorage 'dw_pastor_code', it is campus-scoped and device-trust-equivalent) and prefill the field; add one helper line under the input ('Your campus code comes from the Daily Word team'). In MoreScreen.tsx: move App Analytics into the pastor ADMIN group for pastor_leader with copy 'Enter your campus pastor code or admin PIN', and replace both window.prompt() calls with a small inline input row.

recommendations.title: Localize the pastor wizard and sermon surfaces (es/pt-BR/id)
recommendations.detail: The wizard translates exactly four option labels (setup_personal_time etc.) while every header, subtitle, plan option and button in PastorStudyOnboarding.tsx is hard-coded English ('Let's get you set up.', 'Later', 'Back', all step 10-13 options). The 15 pastoral reflection prompts in persona-config.ts are English-only despite the same config carrying full Indonesian AI prompt additions, and SermonNotesScreen's empty state is English-only. A Spanish or Indonesian pastor gets a half-translated flagship flow; t() returning raw keys makes partial coverage worse than none.

ux.flow_walkthrough:
COLD START (futuresdailyword.com, no state): App.tsx mounts with activeTab='home'. First-run users get PathwayPicker as a full-screen welcome (1 tap to pick a persona, or the "Not sure? Church Member" escape), then PushOptIn (1 tap to allow or skip). Sunday visitors (?sermon=1 or ?sunday=1) skip both and land directly on SermonNotesScreen. Everyone else lands on Home with a silent 'congregation' default.

TAB BAR (TabBar.tsx) renders 5 tabs — the visible labels do NOT match the internal ids: home="Home", journal="Notes", messages="Campus", plans="Plans", more="Settings". A 6th TabId 'sermon-notes' exists but has NO tab button — it is reachable ONLY via the ?sermon=1/?sunday=1 deep link (App.tsx:91); when active, no tab shows as selected. LibraryScreen is not a tab at all: it renders inside the Settings tab when MoreScreen's local showLibrary state is true.

HOME (HomeScreen.tsx, 3,707 lines, persona-ordered but actually fixed-order with gates): SeamBar (link out to futures.church) → date/streak chip + ThemeToggle → greeting with a small unlabeled Search icon (1 tap → BibleSearch, an AI concordance overlay whose results hand a prompt to Bible AI — this is the ONLY search entry in the app) → hero reading panel (photo card; with no plan it shows "Browse Plans" → Plans tab; with a plan it shows today's scripture + audio + InlineReflection) → date navigation strip → an UNCONDITIONAL full-width accent "Choose Your Plan" CTA (shows every day even mid-plan; 1 tap → Plans) → persona-gated sections: PastorStudyOnboarding (deeper_study/pastor), comfort verse banner, FeedbackPoll banner (congregation/pastor — the only poll-answer surface, 0 taps), BibleAIPromptSection (1 tap → Bible AI), faith-pathway banner + lesson card (new_to_faith), comfort card, book cards (pastor/comfort → starts a book plan → content reads in Plans), CampusCountBadge, scripture blocks with verse selection → HighlightToolbar (select text → Highlight/Note/Listen/Share/Go Deeper→Bible AI; highlights auto-save as Notes entries — the only way to review highlights later is Notes > All Notes), GreekHebrewPopup (deeper/pastor), Word of the Day, Weekly Word in Review (pastor, Sundays only), commentary (collapsed/expanded). Bible AI is a floating FAB on every tab (Home/Notes mount their own; App mounts one for Campus/Plans/Settings).

NOTES tab (JournalScreen): header "Notes", 4 sub-tabs — Today (today's passages with inline note-taking + ScriptureModal), Sermon (journal entries of type 'sermon' PLUS an embedded SermonNotesScreen weekly fill-in), All Notes (all non-prayer entries incl. auto-saved highlights), Prayer (private prayers; persona-filtered). 2 taps to this week's sermon notes (Notes → Sermon).

CAMPUS tab (MessagesScreen): header "Campus", 3 sub-tabs — Pastor's Corner (campus feed from /api/campus-content; if no campus is set, a text-only dead-end says "Tap the Settings tab below to choose your campus" with no button; pastors get a Post form gated by a pastor code), "Sermons" (actually a SECOND free-form sermon-notes list stored under a DIFFERENT key dw_sermon_notes, disconnected from Journal's sermon entries; its "From Your Pastors" section can never render because PRELOADED_SERMONS=[] and its SermonDetailView + dw_open_sermon_id auto-open shortcut have no live entry point), Prayer Wall (public prayers + PrayerGlobe world map, post form, filter all/my-campus). Prayer wall/globe: 2 taps (Campus → Prayer Wall).

PLANS tab (PlansScreen): hub view = My Campus card (with a DEAD "Prayer Wall" button — no onClick at PlansScreen.tsx:563 — next to a working Live Stream link) → Your Plans → full plan catalog (persona-featured categories) → PASTOR ASHLEY'S BOOKS + PS JANE'S BOOKS (in-app book reader with audio) → ESSAYS ("Knocking on the Door" essay reader — the SAME essay also served by LibraryScreen with different code). A separate "detail" view repeats the browse catalog. So the Plans tab is the de-facto content library: plans + books + essays + campus card.

SETTINGS tab (MoreScreen, ~16 stacked sections): Profile → Persona ("Your Journey") → My Season (Bible AI context) → Bible Translation → Campus picker → Font Size → Language → Daily Reading (chapters/day) → Media (church stream + personal media URL) → Notifications (push toggle + hour, or calendar fallback where push is unsupported) → LIBRARY row ("Essays & Bible Resources" → LibraryScreen: essay + Bible Characters/Locations/Timeline/Word Studies, persona-filtered) → Content (offline KJV download) → Pastoral Care (comfort persona only) → About/Privacy/Terms → Scripture Attribution → Report a Bug → Admin "Poll Results" (pastor persona, code via window.prompt) → "Administrator" App Analytics (visible to EVERY user, PIN via window.prompt) → data notice ("saved on this device only" — stale: cloud backup exists) → SeamFooter. Reference material is therefore 3-4 taps deep under a tab labeled Settings (Settings → Library → item → sub-item).

BACK/GESTURE: navigateTab mirrors tab changes into history.pushState({dwTab}), and popstate pops the in-memory tab stack — so browser/Android/gesture back moves between TABS and exits at root. But NO sub-view participates in history: Library sub-pages, Plans book/essay/detail readers, Journal entry editor, Campus sermon detail, sub-tab switches, Bible AI panel, search overlay, and MoreScreen's Library/Poll/Analytics swaps are all plain useState. A back-swipe while 3 levels deep in an essay throws the user out of the entire tab (or out of the app at root). The popstate handler also ignores direction and event.state — pressing the browser FORWARD button fires popstate and pops the stack, i.e. Forward navigates backwards. There are no URLs at all (single path; refresh always lands on Home; nothing is shareable/bookmarkable except ?sermon=1 and ?embed=1). Tapping the already-active tab does nothing (does not close Library or reset sub-tabs).

ORPHANS/DEAD (code-verified): PlansScreen Prayer Wall button (no handler); dw_open_sermon_id reader with no setter anywhere; PRELOADED_SERMONS=[] making SermonDetailView unreachable; 10 of 12 extracted components in src/sections (GreetingSection, ComfortCardSection, BookCardsSection, PollBannerSection, WordOfDaySection, WeeklyReviewSection, CampusCountSection, DailyQuoteSection, CongregationStatsSection + HomeContext) never imported by any screen; sectionOrder keys 'devotion_scripture' (gate exists, no persona has it) and 'congregation_stats' (pastor persona lists it, nothing renders it); i18n string 'sunday_service' defined and unused. No export-your-data feature exists anywhere (sharing is per-selection via the highlight toolbar only).

recommendations.title: Make Plans the single 'Read' hub; move Library out of Settings
recommendations.detail: Reading material is split across two unrelated places: books and the 'Knocking on the Door' essay live in the Plans tab (PlansScreen hub sections), while the SAME essay plus Bible Characters/Locations/Timeline/Word Studies live in LibraryScreen, buried 2+ taps deep behind a row labeled 'Essays & Bible Resources' inside a tab labeled 'Settings'. Nobody looks for reading content under Settings, and the duplicate essay reader (two different implementations of the same content) will drift. The Plans tab already IS the content library — its label just undersells it.
recommendations.concrete_change: 1) Rename the plans tab label in TabBar.tsx TAB_LABELS from 'Plans' to 'Read' (en; es 'Leer', pt 'Ler', id 'Baca') and keep the TabId 'plans' unchanged so nothing else moves. 2) In PlansScreen hub view, add a 'Reference' section (Characters/Locations/Timeline/Word Studies) reusing LibraryScreen's data views — simplest increment: render <LibraryScreen> from a PlansScreen state flag exactly the way MoreScreen does today. 3) Delete PlansScreen's own essay-reader states (activeEssay/essayTOC/essaySection, PlansScreen.tsx:199-204, 327-350, 461+) and route its ESSAYS card into the same LibraryScreen essay reader, so one essay implementation remains. 4) Keep the Settings > LIBRARY row for one release as a pass-through, then remove it.

recommendations.title: Put sub-views into browser history so back/gesture doesn't eject the user
recommendations.detail: Only tab switches push history (App.tsx navigateTab). Every drill-down — Plans book/essay reader, plan detail, Library item, Journal entry editor, Campus sermon/prayer sub-views, MoreScreen's Library/Poll/Analytics swaps — is plain useState. On Android hardware back or iOS back-swipe (both wired to popstate), a user 3 levels deep in an essay is thrown out of the entire tab, and at history root out of the app. Additionally App.tsx's onPop ignores event.state, so the browser FORWARD button also pops the tab stack — Forward acts as Back. For a PWA whose primary audience is mobile congregation members, back-gesture data-context loss is the single biggest navigation defect.
recommendations.concrete_change: In App.tsx, export a tiny helper (e.g. pushSubView(closeFn)) that does history.pushState({dwSub:true},'') and registers the close callback; make the existing onPop close the newest registered sub-view first and only pop the tab stack when none is open. Adopt it at the six highest-value spots: MoreScreen showLibrary/showPollDashboard/showAnalytics, PlansScreen showPlanDetail/activeBook/activeEssay, LibraryScreen activeItem/essaySection, JournalScreen editingEntry, MessagesScreen viewingSermon, and the BibleAI open panel. Also make onPop read event.state?.dwTab and jump to it (instead of blind pop) so Forward stops navigating backwards. Pure SPA-state change — no router, no URL scheme, no invariant touched.

recommendations.title: Collapse the three sermon-note surfaces into Notes > Sermon
recommendations.detail: Sermon notes exist in three places with two disconnected storage keys: (a) Notes > Sermon tab = journal entries of type 'sermon' + embedded SermonNotesScreen weekly fill-in (canonical, cloud-synced via the journal tombstone merge); (b) Campus > 'Sermons' sub-tab = a separate free-form list under dw_sermon_notes (MessagesScreen SermonNotesPanel) whose headline feature — 'From Your Pastors' preloaded sermons — can never render because PRELOADED_SERMONS is an empty array (src/data/sermons.ts:31), making SermonDetailView and the dw_open_sermon_id shortcut (reader at MessagesScreen.tsx:788, no setter anywhere) dead code; (c) the hidden 'sermon-notes' TabId reachable only by deep link. Users who take sermon notes in Campus never see them in Notes and vice versa — fragmented pastoral data.
recommendations.concrete_change: 1) In JournalScreen's Sermon tab, ALSO render legacy dw_sermon_notes entries (read-only list above 'My sermon notes') — additive render, do NOT migrate/delete the key (deletes are tombstones; applyMisc is fill-only). 2) Remove the 'Sermons' sub-tab from MessagesScreen (keep Pastor's Corner + Prayer Wall), replacing it with a one-line link card 'Your sermon notes moved to Notes → Sermon'. 3) Delete SermonNotesPanel's dead plumbing: the dw_open_sermon_id effect, SermonDetailView, and the PRELOADED_SERMONS branch. 4) Keep the 'sermon-notes' deep-link TabId as-is (Sunday QR flow depends on it).

recommendations.title: Wire or remove the dead Prayer Wall button in Plans
recommendations.detail: The My Campus card in the Plans hub renders a styled 'Prayer Wall' button with NO onClick (PlansScreen.tsx:563-565) beside a working Live Stream link. Every tap on it silently does nothing — a visible broken promise on a card users actually see once they've set a campus.
