If that plumbing is deferred, delete the button — a dead control is worse than an absent one.

recommendations.title: Give the Campus empty state a real action instead of instructions
recommendations.detail: Campus is a first-class tab, but until a campus is chosen its default sub-tab shows only text: 'Tap the Settings tab below to choose your campus' (MessagesScreen.tsx:~160). That's a two-hop instruction (find Settings tab, scroll to the 5th section, use the dropdown) at exactly the moment of highest intent. Same dead-end pattern as the More > Media row ('Set your campus above...').
recommendations.concrete_change: Render the campus <select> (the same CAMPUSES optgroup dropdown MoreScreen uses — extract it into components/CampusSelect.tsx) directly inside the Campus tab empty state, saving via the existing saveProfile/requireEmail path. Reuse it in MoreScreen to avoid duplication. One component, two call sites.

recommendations.title: Make Home's plan CTA state-aware
recommendations.detail: The full-width accent 'Choose Your Plan' button (HomeScreen.tsx:~2063) renders unconditionally every day, even for users mid-plan whose hero already shows today's reading — it competes with the hero's own 'Browse Plans' empty-state CTA and trains banner blindness on the app's strongest visual weight. Persona config already tells us plan state (todaysPlanPassages / activePlans are in scope at that point).
recommendations.concrete_change: Gate the button: when the user has no active plan or reading slots, keep 'Choose Your Plan'; when a plan is active, either hide it (hero + Plans tab already cover the path) or swap to a quiet secondary 'Manage plans' text link. One conditional around the existing JSX block; no restyle.

recommendations.title: Delete the orphaned src/sections components and inert persona keys
recommendations.detail: 10 of the 12 components in src/sections (GreetingSection, ComfortCardSection, BookCardsSection, PollBannerSection, WordOfDaySection, WeeklyReviewSection, CampusCountSection, DailyQuoteSection, CongregationStatsSection, plus HomeContext) are imported by nothing — HomeScreen imports only BibleAIPromptSection and ComfortVerseBannerSection and renders the rest inline. They're stale forks (BookCardsSection even has different colors than the live inline version) that will mislead the next extraction pass. Related config rot: sectionOrder key 'devotion_scripture' gates a block no persona can ever show (HomeScreen.tsx:2347, confirmed), 'congregation_stats' is promised in pastor_leader's sectionOrder but nothing renders it, and i18n string 'sunday_service' (HomeScreen.tsx:210) is never used.
recommendations.concrete_change: Delete the 10 unused files from src/sections and prune sections/index.ts to the two live exports (keep HomeContext only if BibleAIPromptSection/ComfortVerseBannerSection use it — verify imports first). Remove the devotion_scripture render block, the congregation_stats sectionOrder entry (or implement it — owner's call; removal is the honest default), and the sunday_service string. Pure dead-code removal; tsc -b proves zero behavior change.

recommendations.title: Rebalance Settings: demote Administrator, group admin tools, fix the stale data notice
recommendations.detail: MoreScreen stacks ~16 sections; the 'Administrator > App Analytics' row is shown to ALL ~144 users (window.prompt PIN gate) though it serves ~1 person, while genuinely popular controls (Language, Notifications) sit below heavier sections. The closing data notice — 'Your notes and reading progress are saved on this device only' — is factually wrong since cloud backup shipped (user-sync.js), and actively undermines trust in the sync the app now performs.
recommendations.concrete_change: 1) Merge 'Admin' (Poll Results, pastor-gated) and 'Administrator' (Analytics) into one 'Admin' section, and reveal the Analytics row only for pastor_leader persona OR after a long-press on the version line (keep the PIN prompt as the real gate). 2) Reorder: Profile → Your Journey → Notifications → Language → Bible Translation → Font Size → Campus → Daily Reading → My Season → Media → Content → About/Attribution → Bug → Admin. 3) Rewrite the data notice: 'Your notes back up to your account when you're online. Clearing browser data before a sync can lose recent changes.' Copy + ordering only — no logic or invariant touched.

recommendations.title: Surface Bible Search beyond one unlabeled icon
recommendations.detail: BibleSearch (AI concordance → tappable passages → Bible AI) is one of the app's most differentiated features, yet its only entry is a small unlabeled magnifier beside the Home greeting (HomeScreen.tsx:1450). It's invisible on every other tab, and users scanning for 'search the Bible' in the Plans/reading context find nothing.
recommendations.concrete_change: 1) Add a visible 'Search the Bible' row/pill at the top of the PlansScreen hub (and, post-R1, the Read hub) that opens the same BibleSearch overlay — lift showSearch into App or fire a window CustomEvent ('dw-open-search') that HomeScreen-mounted BibleSearch listens for; the App-level mount pattern used for BibleAI is the template. 2) Give the Home icon an aria-visible text label ('Search') matching the tab-bar label style.

recommendations.title: Reset sub-state when the active tab is re-tapped
recommendations.detail: Tapping the tab you're already on does nothing: a user lost inside Settings > Library (or a Plans book reader) instinctively taps the tab icon to get back to the tab's root, and the app ignores it. Standard mobile-tab convention is re-tap = return to root/scroll to top; its absence compounds the R2 back-navigation gap because MoreScreen's sub-screens replace the whole screen with no header route back to Settings visible.
recommendations.concrete_change: In App.tsx onTabChange, when id === activeTab dispatch window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('dw-tab-reset', {detail: id})); each screen with sub-state (MoreScreen showLibrary/showPollDashboard/showAnalytics, PlansScreen showPlanDetail/activeBook/activeEssay, JournalScreen editingEntry, MessagesScreen viewingSermon) listens and clears its sub-state + scrolls to top. Matches the app's existing CustomEvent bus convention (dw-journal-updated, dw-lang-changed).

ux.flow_walkthrough:
DISCOVERY (futures.church, per code): A visitor can meet Daily Word at 7 live touchpoints. (1) Homepage: HomeRhythms (components/home/HomeRhythms.tsx), the third-act rhythms grid near the very bottom of a long homepage (after HomeMoDPromo and HomeBooksOffer). Card 2 of 3: BookOpen icon, title "Daily Word", caption "One short reading. Every morning. In your inbox.", CTA "subscribe" -> /daily-word, same tab. All four locales (en/es/pt/id) promise an inbox/email product. (2) Nav: Resources dropdown -> "Daily Word" (2 taps, target=_blank new tab; components/layout/Nav.tsx line 74). (3) Footer "Grow" -> "Daily Word" -> /daily-word-app (a DIFFERENT route: iframe embed page). (4) /jesus "keep going" card -> /daily-word (new tab). (5) 404 page card "Daily Word — One scripture, every morning" -> /daily-word. (6) Milo AI: milo-knowledge.ts says "Free daily devotional… Email or app… Subscribe at /daily-word"; PAGE_CONTEXT says "One short email a day… Help them subscribe"; route-editorial keywords include "morning email". (7) /press facts list: "Daily Word subscribers: 300,000+" (verified live). Sitemap deliberately omits /daily-word (noindex doorway intent). CRITICAL STRUCTURAL FACT: the church repo contains a full marketing doorway — app/daily-word/page.tsx (DailyWordPageClient hero "One word. One breath. One day", Milo chips, 3 signup bands claiming "300,000+ people wake up to this", 30-day archive) plus app/daily-word/[date]/ article pages with Article JSON-LD and a Daily Word opengraph-image claiming "Joining 80,000+ others" — but ALL of it is DEAD: netlify.toml lines 68-78 force-proxy (status 200, force=true) /daily-word and /daily-word/* to futures-daily-word.netlify.app before Next ever runs. Verified live: futures.church/daily-word returns the SPA's index.html (title "Futures Daily Word") with the path-scoped DAILY_WORD_CSP from middleware.ts correctly attached. DailyWordCapture.tsx and content/daily-word.json (subscriberCount 312,000, entries frozen at 2026-04-18) are unreferenced/dead. So nothing that actually SELLS the app ever renders; the live entry copy sells an email devotional that does not exist.

HAND-OFF, ENTRY A (homepage card, same tab): 1 click -> full-page load of the SPA. Church header/nav/footer disappear entirely. Branding continuity is decent: the app's SeamBar (src/components/Seam.tsx) shows the Futures wordmark + "Daily Word", ivory/terracotta look is family-consistent. First run: PathwayPicker full-screen gate (1 tap, with a "Not sure -> Church Member" escape), then PushOptIn full-screen gate. On this origin pushSupported() is false (push.ts gates to futuresdailyword.com/www/localhost), so the user is offered "Add to my calendar" (ICS recurring event) or "Maybe later" — 2 more decisions before content. Email gate is deferred to the first commit action (journal/plan/prayer). GETTING BACK IS BROKEN: SeamBar's "Futures Church ↗" and the More-screen SeamFooter's "Back to Futures Church" both point at CHURCH_DAILY_WORD_URL = https://futures.church/daily-word — which the forced proxy serves as… the app again. Every in-app "back to church" affordance is a self-loop (the Seam comment shows it predates the forced proxy). Browser back is the only real way home. ENTRY B (nav / jesus, new tab): same app experience, but the church tab survives in the background — accidental, not designed, "way back". ENTRY C (footer -> /daily-word-app): DailyWordEmbed renders a fixed overlay with a slim church bar (wordmark -> "/") and an <a> labeled "← Futures Church" that actually hrefs /daily-word — i.e. the "back to church" control loads the full-page APP. Below it, an iframe of futuresdailyword.com/?embed=1 (app hides its seam via IS_EMBEDDED). Two hidden traps in this route: (a) inside the cross-origin iframe location.hostname IS futuresdailyword.com, so pushSupported() returns TRUE and PushOptIn offers real notifications — but Notification.requestPermission() is auto-denied in a cross-origin iframe without permission delegation (the iframe's allow list has no notifications), so "Turn on daily reminders" silently fails and the calendar fallback is never offered; (b) modern browsers partition third-party storage, so everything the user builds inside the embed (journal, streak, plans) lives in a partitioned localStorage bucket invisible to a later direct visit to futuresdailyword.com — a third, orphaned identity for a localStorage-first app whose #1 risk is data loss. Three entry points therefore produce three different storage identities (church-origin, partitioned-iframe, app-origin), reconciled only if the user enters the same email (cloudSync syncOnStartup is email-keyed).

NUDGE TO THE NATIVE ORIGIN: on futures.church/daily-word the ONLY mention that the real app (push, install) lives at futuresdailyword.com is one plain-text, non-hyperlinked sentence buried in More -> notifications: "Adds a recurring daily event to your calendar. Install the app from futuresdailyword.com for in-app notifications." (MoreScreen.tsx:771). PushOptIn's calendar variant never mentions it. Nothing warns that switching origins needs the same email to carry data across.

SHARED/BOOKMARKED LINKS: futures.church/daily-word shared -> scraper receives the SPA's index.html: og:title "Futures Daily Word — Your Daily Bible Reading Companion", og:image https://futuresdailyword.com/og-image.png (200 OK), og:url + rel=canonical pointing at futuresdailyword.com — a coherent generic app card, no per-day content. futures.church/daily-word/<anything> (including the dead [date] article URLs) -> SPA shell, the app ignores the path, user lands on Home; no 404, no message. futuresdailyword.com/<anything> -> SPA fallback to Home (the dead church page's "futuresdailyword.com/archive" promise lands nowhere specific). ?sermon= / ?sunday= query deep-links survive both origins (query strings forwarded by the proxy). In-app shares (HomeScreen.tsx:2677, NewBelieverLessonCard.tsx:132) always share https://futuresdailyword.com — correctly funneling recipients to the installable origin. /daily-word-app shared -> og:title "Daily Word — Futures Church" but inherits the generic church twitter/og image ("One family. 25 campuses. 5 countries"), not a Daily Word card. One more trap: the church proxies /manifest.json to the app's manifest (start_url "/"), so a visitor who uses the browser's Install/Add-to-Home-Screen on futures.church/daily-word gets a "Daily Word" icon that opens https://futures.church/ — the church HOMEPAGE, not the app.

VERDICT: the current entry does not sell the app. Every live surface describes a subscription email ("in your inbox", "subscribe", Milo's "one short email a day", press's 300,000+ subscribers) while the actual product — a personalized reading app with plans, journal, audio Bible, Bible AI, streaks and reminders, ~144 real users — is described nowhere a visitor can see. The one page that did sell it is dead code behind the forced proxy, and its fabricated numbers (300k/312k/80k) are one broken redirect away from rendering in public.

recommendations.title: Fix the app's 'Back to Futures Church' self-loop
recommendations.detail: SeamBar ('Futures Church ↗') and SeamFooter ('Back to Futures Church') both link to CHURCH_DAILY_WORD_URL = https://futures.church/daily-word, which the church's forced Netlify proxy serves as the Daily Word app itself. On BOTH origins, every in-app route back to the church opens another copy of the app — the single worst hand-off defect in the journey. The Seam.tsx comment shows this predates the forced proxy (it expected a church doorway page at that URL).
recommendations.concrete_change: In futures-daily-word src/components/Seam.tsx, change the CHURCH_DAILY_WORD_URL fallback from 'https://futures.church/daily-word' to 'https://futures.church' (and set VITE_CHURCH_DAILY_WORD_URL accordingly in Netlify env if present). recommendations.title: Make the church entry copy sell the product that exists
recommendations.detail: Homepage HomeRhythms card says 'One short reading. Every morning. In your inbox.' with CTA 'subscribe' (all four locales); Milo's two brains say 'Email or app… one short email a day… help them subscribe'; the 404 card says 'One scripture, every morning'. Homepage + Milo are critical-static/owner-locked — get Ashley's sign-off on the strings first.

recommendations.title: Retire the /daily-word-app iframe route (or fix its two traps now)
recommendations.detail: The footer's only Daily Word link goes to /daily-word-app, a cross-origin iframe of futuresdailyword.com. Inside it, pushSupported() sees the app origin and offers real notifications, but Notification.requestPermission() is auto-denied in a cross-origin iframe (no delegation in the allow list) — the opt-in silently fails and the calendar fallback never triggers. Browser storage partitioning also gives embed users a third, orphaned localStorage identity that a later direct visit can't see (data-loss risk for a localStorage-first app). And the bar's escape link is mislabeled: '← Futures Church' hrefs /daily-word (the full-page app), not the church.
recommendations.concrete_change: futures-church-web: point Footer.tsx's Grow link at /daily-word (matching nav/homepage — one consistent entry), and delete app/daily-word-app/page.tsx + components/streams/DailyWordEmbed.tsx (or, if the route must stay, change the '← Futures Church' anchor to href='/' and add allow='notifications' delegation — but retiring is better; the fewer origins holding user data, the safer).

recommendations.title: Bridge church-proxy users to the native origin — with the same-email safety rail
recommendations.detail: Push can never work on futures.church/daily-word (deliberate /sw.js kill-switch — invariant), so church-entry users permanently get the weaker calendar experience. The only pointer to the real origin is one unlinked sentence buried in More → notifications. Users who DO follow it and switch origins start with empty localStorage unless they enter the same email (cloud restore is email-keyed) — the nudge must carry that instruction or it becomes a perceived data-loss event.
recommendations.concrete_change: futures-daily-word: (1) in PushOptIn's calendar variant add a secondary line + link: 'Want real notifications and a home-screen app? Continue at futuresdailyword.com — sign in with the same email and everything comes with you.' (2) make the MoreScreen.tsx:771 sentence a real <a href="https://futuresdailyword.com"> with the same same-email note; (3) optionally show a one-time dismissible banner on the church host only (location.hostname check, dw_ key to remember dismissal, synced via syncMisc). Keep the calendar fallback exactly as-is; never auto-redirect.

recommendations.title: Remove the fabricated Daily Word numbers from live and dormant church surfaces
recommendations.detail: futures.church/press publicly states 'Daily Word subscribers: 300,000+' (verified live); the dormant doorway strings claim '300,000+ people wake up to this' (dailyword.signup.* in all four dicts), content/daily-word.json says subscriberCount 312,000, and the Daily Word opengraph-image says 'Joining 80,000+ others'. The app has ~144 real users and no email product. A press-facts page carrying an invented metric is a reputational risk and violates the canon discipline the site enforces elsewhere.
recommendations.concrete_change: futures-church-web: run the futures-canon check on 'Daily Word subscribers'; absent a verified figure, delete the FACTS row in app/press/page.tsx (and its i18n keys). Purge the 300k/312k/80k strings from lib/i18n/dicts/*, content/daily-word.json, and app/daily-word/opengraph-image.tsx as part of DW-UX-06.

recommendations.title: Delete (or consciously resurrect) the dead /daily-word doorway in the church repo
recommendations.detail: app/daily-word/page.tsx, DailyWordPageClient, app/daily-word/[date]/* (30 frozen sample devotionals dated April 2026), both opengraph-image.tsx files, DailyWordCapture.tsx and content/daily-word.json are fully shadowed by the forced Netlify proxy — none of it ever serves. It is not harmless: if the forced redirect is ever edited or fails, futures.church/daily-word instantly renders a fake product page (300k social proof, a signup for a nonexistent 5am email, an archive frozen in April). It also misleads every future contributor (and Milo's route scanner) about what /daily-word is.
recommendations.concrete_change: futures-church-web: delete app/daily-word/** , app/daily-word-app (per DW-UX-03), components/streams/DailyWordPageClient.tsx, components/streams/DailyWordEmbed.tsx, components/sections/DailyWordCapture.tsx, content/daily-word.json, and the dailyword.* i18n keys; keep the netlify.toml proxy + middleware DAILY_WORD_CSP untouched (invariants). If Ashley instead wants a real marketing doorway, rebuild it at a non-shadowed path (e.g. /daily-word-about) with truthful copy and a single 'Open the app' CTA — never behind the proxied prefix.

recommendations.title: Defuse the install trap: church-proxy manifest opens the church homepage
recommendations.detail: The app's index.html links /manifest.json root-absolute; the church proxies that path to the app's manifest (start_url '/'). Resolved against futures.church, a browser Install / Add-to-Home-Screen from futures.church/daily-word creates a 'Daily Word' icon that launches https://futures.church/ — the church homepage, not the app. A user who 'installed Daily Word' and gets the church site will conclude the app is broken.
recommendations.concrete_change: futures-daily-word public/manifest.json: set "start_url": "https://futuresdailyword.com/". Per the manifest spec a cross-origin start_url is discarded and falls back to the document URL — so on the church proxy an install now opens futures.church/daily-word (the app), while on futuresdailyword.com it stays exactly as today. One line; the /sw.js kill-switch and proxy rules stay untouched.

recommendations.title: Give Daily Word a discoverable, consistent placement on the church site
recommendations.detail: The church's flagship daily-engagement product is a third-level item in a 'Resources' dropdown (2 taps, alongside Selah and Wellness), a bottom-of-page rhythms card, and a footer link that currently goes to a different route. Selah — a comparable product — gets the same rhythms slot plus richer treatment. Nothing above the fold anywhere invites a visitor into a daily habit with the church.
recommendations.concrete_change: futures-church-web (nav/footer are critical-static — Ashley sign-off required): (a) make all entries target the same /daily-word URL with the same new-tab behavior (today: nav=new tab, homepage card=same tab, footer=different route); (b) propose to Ashley promoting 'Daily Word' out of Resources — either a top-level nav item or first item in the dropdown — and adding one sentence of what it is ('Scripture, reflection and a question to carry — free every morning') wherever it appears (jesus page card, 404 helper already close). Pair with DW-UX-02 copy so every touchpoint sells the same true product.
